newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA raises offer for Value Health.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA raises offer for Value Health.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp. has agreed to raise its friendly takeover offer for Value Health Inc. to about $1.12 billion and pay cash instead of stock, the companies said Tuesday.

The revision, which adds about $50 million to the value of the merger, came after Columbia/HCA's stock tumbled in recent weeks on news of a federal probe into its El Paso, Texas facilities. The health care company has said it is cooperating with federal agents and has not been informed of allegations.

Value Health also said it received and rejected a rival offer from MedPartners Inc., which proposed exchanging 1.112 shares of its common stock for each Value Health share in a tax-free pooling of interests.

Under the revised deal, Columbia will now offer $20.50 in cash, instead of 0.58 share of its common stock, for each Value Health share. The previous plan had a market value of $19.58 per Value Health share, or about $1.07 billion, based on Tuesday's stock prices.

"I think the uncertainty of what's happening in the stock is a reason. We wanted to take as much uncertainty out of the deal for our shareholders as was possible," said Value Health spokeswoman Judith Hyfield-Starr.
Value Health's stock gained $2.375 to $20.125, while Columbia/HCA rose $2.50 to $33.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.

The original Columbia pact, which was valued at $1.3 billion when it was announced in January, did not have a provision to protect Value Health shareholders in case of a stock decline, Hyfield-Starr said.
Value Health, based in Avon, Conn., said other terms of the revised deal were essentially unchanged.
In rejecting the MedPartners offer, Value Health cited several factors, including a lack of price protection, and the existence of conditions.

Value Health said the MedPartners proposal was subject to the negotiation of a definitive agreement, final approval of MedPartners' board and the completion of financial and legal reviews. MedPartners' stock fell 50 cents to $19.875 on the NYSE.
